items.title: 9 घंटे की आनाकानी के बाद पुलिस ने दर्ज की अजीत भारती के खिलाफ एफआईआर
items.summary: दिल्ली के नॉर्थ एवेन्यू थाने में यूट्यूबर अजीत भारती के खिलाफ एससीएसटी एक्ट, आईटी एक्ट और बीएनएस की गंभीर धाराओं में एफआईआर दर्ज की गई है. भारती ने अपने यूट्यूब पर एक वीडियो में डॉ. आंबेडकर, नगीना से सांसद चंद्रशेखर आज़ाद और दलित समाज के बारे में टिप्पणियां की थी. साथ ही उन्होंने दलित समाज की महिलाओं को लेकर बेहद आपत्तिजनक यौन टिप्पणियां भी की. इसके बाद आजाद समाज पार्टी के कार्यकर्ताओं ने 23 अगस्त रविवार की देर शाम थाने में लंबी जद्दोजहद के बाद एफआईआर दर्ज कराई है. मामले में शिकायतकर्ता और आजाद समाज पार्टी के दिल्ली प्रदेश अध्यक्ष बालकराम बौद्ध के मुताबिक, भारती ने अपने यूट्यूब पर 'आरक्षण हटाओ नौटंकी' और जंतर-मंतर पर हुए प्रदर्शनों के मुद्दे पर चर्चा करते हुए आपत्तिजनक टिप्पणियां कीं. भारती ने इस वीडियो में जातिसूचक शब्दों के साथ-साथ चंद्रशेखर की शक्ल और उनकी मूंछों पर थूकने की भी बात कही है. हालांकि, अजीत भारती के यूट्यूब चैनल पर अब यह वीडियो उपलब्ध नहीं है. इस एफआईआर में तीन अलग-अलग कानूनों की कुल 9 धाराएं लगाई गई हैं. इसमें अनुसूचित जाति एवं अनुसूचित जनजाति (अत्याचार निवारण) अधिनियम, 1989 की धारा 3(1)(r), 3(1)(s), 3(1)(u), 3(1)(v), 3(1)(w)(ii) और 3(2)(va) के तहत मुकदमा दर्ज किया गया है. इसके अलावा दूसरा भारतीय न्याय संहिता, 2023 की धारा 196 (1)(c) और 351(3) लगाई गई है. साथ ही सूचना एवं प्रौद्योगिकी अधिनियम, 2000 की धारा 67 के तहत मुकदमा दर्ज किया गया है. शिकायतकर्ता की मांग है कि आरोपी के खिलाफ सख्त कानूनी कार्रवाई की जाए और संबंधित सोशल मीडिया अकाउंट्स से इस वीडियो को हटवाया जाए. वहीं, इस एफआईआर के बाद अजीत भारती ने एक्स पर लिखा , "मैं जानता हूं कि दिल्ली पुलिस के नॉर्थ एवेन्यू में आजाद समाज पार्टी वालों ने कितना दवाब दे कर रात के बारह बजे यह एफआईआर लिखवाई है, जो कोर्ट में दो मिनट नहीं टिकेगी. एक भी धारा ऐसी नहीं है, जो होल्ड करेगी…. यदि ऐसा कमेंट फिर मेरे वीडियो पर आया तो मैं पुनः उसी तरीके से उत्तर दूंगा जो मैंने दिया." बता दें कि जंतर-मंतर पर 21 अगस्त को ‘आरक्षण हटाओ आंदोलन’ (आरएचए) के बैनर/सोशल मीडिया अभियान के तहत बुलाया गया था. यहां प्रदर्शनकारियों ने जाति आधारित आरक्षण और यूजीसी के इक्विटी नियमों का विरोध किया था. इसी सिलसिले में अजीत भारती भी जंतर-मंतर पहुंचे थे. जहां उन्होंने लोगों को संबोधित भी किया. इसके बाद उन्होंने वहां आए लोगों का धन्यवाद करते हुए अपने यूट्यूब चैनल पर लाइव किया. लाइव के दौरान वह कमेंट पढ़कर उनका जवाब दे रहे थे. इसी लाइव बातबीत के दौरान किसी ने कमेंट किया कि अजीत भाई अपनी बहन की शादी एमपी चंद्रशेखर से कर दो, रिजर्वेशन खत्म हो जाएगा. इसी का जवाब देते हुए अजीत अपना आपा खो बैठे और उन्होंने पूरे दलित समाज को घेर लिया और आपत्तिजनक एवं अश्लील टिप्पणी की. इस पूरे मामले पर आजाद समाज पाटी के दिल्ली प्रदेश प्रभारी महेश पहवाल न्यूज़ल

items.title: A year after Israeli strikes killed journalists at a hospital, no one has been held accountable
items.summary: It’s been a year since Israeli soldiers killed 22 Palestinians , including journalists and rescue workers, in a double strike on a hospital in Gaza. No one has been held accountable. Israeli officials said the target was a suspected Hamas camera on the roof of Nasser Hospital. Among those killed were Reuters cameraman Hussam al-Masri and Mariam Dagga , a visual journalist who worked for The Associated Press and other news organisations. Despite repeated requests by AP , the army hasn’t provided details about the investigation or a timeline for when it could be completed. Rights groups say Israel rarely holds troops accountable for killing Palestinians, pointing to long investigations that rarely lead to prosecution . As global outrage over the August 25, 2025, strikes grew, the Israeli military said that in addition to taking out the camera, six of those killed were linked to Hamas, without providing evidence. But an Israeli soldier, speaking on condition of anonymity for fear of retribution, now says the military could find no evidence linking the camera, which belonged to al-Masri, to Hamas. The soldier, who was privy to discussions surrounding the military’s response, said none of the six was the intended target of the strikes. AP sent detailed questions to the military about the allegations, as well as other questions about the strikes. The military didn’t address the questions but said the incident is being examined and findings will be transferred to the Military Advocate General’s Corps to reach a verdict on whether to open a criminal investigation. It didn’t provide a timeline. AP reported at the time that one of the six Israel said was linked to Hamas wasn’t on the hospital’s list of casualties and two others were medical or emergency personnel. That, along with the soldier’s account, raises serious questions about Israel’s rationale for the strikes. Why did troops fail to identify the cameraman as al-Masri, even though journalists were known to film at the hospital? Why did they strike a second time, causing most of the deaths and raising accusations of a “double tap” attack on first responders, which would be a war crime? AP and Reuters released a statement Tuesday calling again for Israel to provide a full explanation of the strikes. items.title: Banke Bihari Temple: Supreme Court says all donations must go directly to temple treasury
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday directed that all donations made to the Banke Bihari Temple in Vrindavan be deposited through the temple’s donation boxes or online, directly into the temple treasury. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, “Let there be no doubt, and we accordingly direct that every penny of donation must come through the donation boxes or online [into the] temple treasury. Any impediment created by sevayats (temple servants) or anyone else shall be viewed very seriously." Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The Court also directed the Temple’s managing committee to introduce a transparent mechanism for receiving donations and take all necessary steps to prevent malpractices. The directions were passed in the broader dispute concerning the management and administration of the Banke Bihari Temple, including the manner in which its funds are handled and the constitution of a committee to oversee its affairs. The dispute arose after the Uttar Pradesh government brought the Temple’s management under a statutory framework through the Uttar Pradesh Shri Banke Bihari Ji Temple Trust Ordinance, 2025. The move sought to replace the 1939 Scheme of Management, which has long governed the administration and rituals of the temple, including provisions concerning darshan, religious practices and temple finances. The proposed State-controlled trust had led to questions over the extent of government involvement in the management of religious institutions. In August 2025, the Supreme Court had set up a high-powered committee headed by former Allahabad High Court Justice Ashok Kumar to oversee the temple’s day-to-day functioning. The committee was tasked with ensuring basic amenities for devotees, including drinking water, washrooms, shelters, crowd-management corridors and facilities for vulnerable devotees, besides planning the development of the temple and its surroundings, including land acquisition where necessary. Notably, in May 2025 , the Court had permitted the Uttar Pradesh government to use temple funds to acquire five acres of land around the temple for corridor development, subject to the land being registered in the name of the deity. items.title: Flash floods an 'act of God', ensuing damage to rented building can't be basis of cheating case: J&K High Court
items.summary: Damage caused a building due to flash floods cannot be blamed on its landlord, observed the Jammu and Kashmir High Court recently while quashing a cheating case filed against the landlord and trustees of a school by a person who had taken over its management [ Ghulam Rasool Rather & Ors. v. UT of J&K ]. The woman who had taken over the management claimed that the school's trustees had failed to disclose structural deficiencies in the school building when it was handed over to her. She, therefore, accused the school's trustees and the building's landlord of cheating her. Justice Sanjay Dhar , however, observed that the primary basis for such an allegation was the damage caused to the building after flash floods that occurred in the area in 2013. Flash floods are an act of God and cannot, by itself, form the basis of a criminal cheating case, the Court held. "Merely because water of flash floods entered the school building and it caused damage to the school building does not make out a case of cheating of the petitioners (school trustees, landlord of building). The petitioners/trustees only happen to be the managers of the school and they had transferred the management of the school along with its goodwill to respondent No. 2 (complainant). They had nothing to do with the quality of the school building nor were they responsible for flash floods, which were an act of God," the Court said. Justice Sanjay Dhar The Court reiterated that to constitute the criminal offence of cheating under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code (now replaced by Section 318 of the BNS, 2023), there must be a fraudulent or dishonest intention. Mere breach of contract or subsequent difficulties cannot automatically give rise to criminal prosecution, it added. The High Court was hearing two petitions to quash a criminal case filed against several trustees of a school, as well as the landlord in whose property the school was being run. The case was registered on a complaint filed in 2021 by a woman to whom the management of the school was transferred in 2012. The complainant alleged that she was assured that the school had a bright future but later discovered several problems relating to the school premises and its management. She said that around 12 inches of water entered the school building during flash floods in November 2013, causing damage and financial losses. items.title: Supreme Court refuses to interfere with Allahabad HC order on demolition of illegal lawyers’ chambers in Lucknow
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday refused to interfere with an Allahabad High Court order directing the demolition of around 72 illegal lawyers’ chambers near the District and Sessions Court in Lucknow [ Central Bar Association v. State of UP & Ors ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta refused a request to refer the dispute to mediation and advised the lawyers occupying the unauthorised structures to vacate them peacefully. It also told the petitioners that the encroachments could not be allowed to continue merely because those occupying them held positions in the local bar association. “Where is this offending construction situated? You tell us. You occupy the main road, you occupy the open space inside the court premises, raise unauthorised construction and then say I am elected as the president of the association, I am member of the governing body and therefore I have a right to continue. No. All demolitions have to take place,” Justice Nath said. Justice Nath added that he had personally witnessed the extent of such encroachments during his time as a judge in the State. “I have seen it myself when I was there for two years as a senior judge. I know what kind of constructions, how the roads have been obstructed, traffic is completely obstructed. Demolition has to take place,” he said. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta Senior Advocate Adish Aggarwala suggested that an alternative location could be allotted to the lawyers. Justice Nath, however, said that the lawyers could approach the State government for assistance in acquiring land rather than occupying public spaces. “You go and purchase some lands for the lawyers over there. Go and request the State government to provide you a society for that,” he said. When counsel sought that the matter be referred to mediation, Justice Nath rejected the suggestion outright. “Mediation with lawyers! No. Dismissed,” he said. Justice Mehta questioned who was responsible for protecting court premises if lawyers themselves were encroaching upon them. “Who is going to protect the court’s precincts? If it is encroached in this manner. Who is responsible? Lawyers don’t have any kind of qualms,” he said. Justice Mehta then recalled an instance from a visit to a district court in Rajasthan where a lawyer had allegedly converted the parking space meant for district judges into his own chamber. items.title: Supreme Court directs Delhi lawyers bodies to work out women's representation in their governing bodies
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday directed the Delhi High Court Bar Association (DHCBA) and bar bodies of the district courts in the national capital to jointly work out a “structured” and “institutionalised” mechanism for representation of women in their governing bodies for the 2027 Bar elections [Fozia Rahman vs. Bar Council of Delhi and Anr.]. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed that the Coordination Committee of All District Court Bar Associations of Delhi, in consultation with the DHCBA and other bar bodies, to come out with a proposal reflecting an "all-acceptable solution." The Court granted six weeks for consultations to ensure that any impediments or bottlenecks arising during deliberations are discussed and resolved well in time. The Bench told the DHCBA that the matter was one of its leadership, statesmanship, stewardship and "a question of prestige." The Court also expressed confidence that the coordination committee would arrive at a workable solution. "We have no reason to doubt that the coordination committee will come out with an all-acceptable solution, which shall be a structured, institutionalised representation mechanism, so that repeated orders are not required to be passed by this Court," the Court said in its order. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana The Court passed the order on a petition filed by advocate Fozia Rahman seeking reservation for women lawyers in the DHCBA. On December 19, 2024, the top court had passed interim directions reserving, on an experimental basis, the post of treasurer for women across all Delhi bar associations and one post of designated senior member executive for women in the DHCBA. The Court had also reserved 30 percent of executive committee posts for women in all Delhi district court bar associations on an experimental basis. The Court then had underlined the constitutional mandate for women's representation in governance drawing a parallel with panchayats and other local self-government bodies and held that the same principle should extend to the legal fraternity. Senior Advocate Geeta Luthra appeared for the petitioner. items.summary: The Delhi High Court has directed the Delhi Police conduct an inquiry into the case of a woman who has been missing under suspicious circumstances from a spiritual ashram called the Adhyatmik Vidhyalya situated at Rohini in Delhi [ Dumpala Meenavathi and Anr. Vs Union of India and Ors .]. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia passed the order on August 24 on a petition filed by the missing woman’s parents (petitioners). Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia The petitioners alleged that their daughter was being illegally confined by the ashram and sought her release. Two followers of the ashram, who were present in court, meanwhile said that the petitioners' daughter was no longer residing at the ashram. They, however, said that her luggage and belongings were still lying at the ashram. The Court went on to note that there was no clarity on who was running the ashram at present, and the source of funds used for its functioning. “We are of the opinion that the affairs of the aashram and the manner in which they are being run needs to be probed and inquired into," the Court said, adding that this aspect will be examined in the next hearing. Meanwhile, it directed the Delhi Police to register a missing person case and conduct an inquiry into the whereabouts of the petitioners' daughter. The Court has also directed the Station House Officer of the concerned police station branch to be physically present in court during the next hearing to inform it about the outcome of the inquiry. The petitioners had told the Court that the ashram's founder, Virender Dev Dixit, had earlier refused to allow them to speak to their daughter on video call. However, after persistent insistence they were allowed a video call. During this call, they allegedly noted that their daughter's gums were blackened and that she appeared severely weak and malnourished. They alleged that this health deterioration occurred due to forced drug abuse. The petitioners, therefore, also urged the Court to order a medical examination of their daughter at a government hospital to ascertain if she is under the influence of any drug. items.title: West Bengal SIR: Supreme Court seeks ECI data on appeals pending over voters' exclusion/inclusion
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday sought detailed data from the Election Commission of India (ECI) on the number of appeals pending before appellate tribunals challenging exclusion/ inclusion of voters from West Bengal's electoral rolls following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing pleas seeking measures to streamline and expedite the disposal of appeals before the SIR appellate tribunals. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana The Court today directed the ECI to provide a break-up of pending and disposed appeals. The information sought includes: 1. How many appeals are still pending before the appellate tribunals; 2. How many appeals have so far been disposed of, including the nature of relief sought in those appeals; 3. A break-up of the appeals concerning voters whose names have been excluded and those where exclusion of names from the electoral roll has been sought; 4. How many appeals have been allowed and what consequential steps are being taken for updating the electoral rolls pursuant to such orders; and 5. What steps are being taken to streamline the mechanism for disposal of the pending appeals. Pertinently, the Court today said that the SIR process should be concluded and all appeals should be decided at least before the next parliamentary elections in 2029. “ Kindly also propose the suggestions and changes you have made so as to streamline the manner of disposal by the appellate tribunals, ” CJI Kant added, addressing the ECI’s counsel. The order was passed after the petitioners raised concerns that appeals filed by excluded voters must be prioritised by the tribunals over appeals filed by those opposing the inclusion of other voters. They also sought directions for the prompt publication of a supplementary SIR voter list with the names of voters who had successfully challenged their earlier exclusion from the electoral roll. They contended that such measures were necessary to protect the rights of such voters, particularly in view of several upcoming elections. “Municipal elections are coming. They will not be able to cast their votes (if their names are not added to the voter list on time). Then Panchayat elections are coming next year. Then the Lok Sabha elections in 2029. items.title: Drivers move Bombay High Court against Marathi language rule, says livelihood of lakhs under threat
items.summary: Four cab drivers, who operate cabs using mobile cab aggregator apps, have moved the Bombay High Court challenging the Maharashtra government’s decision to make working knowledge of Marathi language compulsory for auto rickshaw, taxi and app‑based cab drivers [Mohd. Kasim Ahmad vs. State of Maharashtra]. The petition filed through advocate Vivek Shukla will be mentioned on August 27 before the acting Chief Justice for urgent directions. The rule was notified via a government notification dated August 12. The plea by the cab drivers argues that the Marathi language rule violates their fundamental rights under Articles 14 (right to equality), 19 (freedom to carry on trade and profession) and 21 (right to life) of the Constitution and is ultra vires the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, which does not prescribe any language requirement for driving licences. As per the plea, "The parent Act (Motor Vehicles Act) confers no power upon the State Government to prescribe working knowledge of any language as a qualification for a driver, as a condition of a badge, or as a condition of a permit, and confers no power to suspend or revoke a badge on such a ground. The impugned notification manufactures a new disqualification and a new ground of suspension and revocation which the parliament never enacted." Lakhs of poor and migrant drivers face imminent suspension of badges and cancellation of permits, threatening their livelihoods if the rule is implemented, the plea states. The PIL has sought an immediate stay on the government notification so as to prevent hardship to nearly 9.65 lakh drivers across Maharashtra. "The scale of the notification is enormous. As stated by the Hon'ble Transport Minister himself in the press, about 9,65,000 rickshaw and taxi permits and badges have been issued in the State so far. As per the Government's own statements, about 1,65,000 non-Marathi speaking drivers attended the 105 day "Hinduhridaysamrat Balasaheb Thackeray Marathi Language Campaign" conducted through the Konkan Marathi Sahitya Parishad and the Mumbai Marathi Sahitya Sangh. Lakhs of drivers remain exposed to notices, suspension and cancellation," the plea claims.

items.title: Better-half will become bitter-half if issues not addressed: Delhi HC acquits man for murder attempt against wife
items.summary: Marriage is paradoxical and a world of extremities, the Delhi High Court recently observed while acquitting a man who was convicted by a trial court for attempting to murder his wife by forcing Baygon Spray (an insecticide) down her throat [Nafe Singh v State] . Justice Vimal Kumar Yadav said that “the best, in no time, becomes worst if not handled carefully”. The Court highlighted recent examples wherein spouses resorted to extreme levels of violence against each other, which was incomprehensible some decades ago. “The better-half becomes the bitter-half if issues are not taken care of and resolved as soon as possible. One of the most beautiful relationships of humans, that is of a husband and wife becomes one of the most terrible when things go wrong in a matrimonial alliance. Time, albeit, is a big healer and tones down a lot of pains in life, however in relationships time taken can also be counterproductive,” the Court stressed. It added that relationships can go in a totally different, undesirable, and unexpected direction if not handled carefully. Delhi High Court There are recent examples in which spouses have resorted to extreme levels of violence against each other, which were incomprehensible some decades ago. The Bench made the observations while allowing an appeal filed by one Nafe Singh against a 2004 order of the trial court sentencing him to three years imprisonment for trying to kill his wife. The couple got married in the year 2000 but the relations soured within a year. In 2001, during a matrimonial dispute, the husband, Nafe Singh, first tried to force his wife to drink Baygon insecticide from a tumbler, and when that failed, he poured it directly down her throat from the container. An FIR was registered and Singh and his mother were charged with offences under Sections 498A (cruelty) for dowry harassment and Section 307 (attempt to murder) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). While the trial court acquitted them of Section 498A, Singh was ordered to undergo three years’ imprisonment for attempt to murder. This led to the appeal before the High Court. items.title: Indian courts show no bias against Chinese companies: Senior Advocate Darius Khambata
items.summary: Indian courts do not discriminate against Chinese companies and have granted them relief by enforcing arbitral awards and freezing assets, Senior Advocate Darius Khambata said on Monday. Khambata was speaking at the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) Symposium 2026 during a panel titled Cross-Border Disputes across China, India and the US: Strategy, Enforcement and Risk . The session was moderated by Clifford Chance partner Kabir Singh . The other panellists were Three Crowns founding partner Luke Sobota , Alibaba Group’s Head of Dispute Resolution and Regulatory Investigations Li Jieyun and Hui Zhong Law Firm Singapore head Hazel Tang . Khambata said that Indian courts remained fair and agnostic about the nationality of parties appearing before them. “ I don’t see any bias in favour of our nationals against any particular national. Chinese companies have won enforcement of awards. They have won Section 9 interim injunctions to freeze assets in Indian courts. ” Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act allows courts to grant interim protection before, during or after arbitral proceedings. Such relief may include orders preserving disputed property, securing the amount involved in the dispute or preventing a party from disposing of its assets. Khambata said that this approach would continue despite the political tensions between India and China. “That should be so. But, of course, the political tensions are resulting in a complete reduction of trading relationships .” Geopolitical and political considerations were presently overriding the economic potential of the two countries, he added. Khambata expressed hope that India and China would eventually expand their commercial engagement. “ I look forward to the day when both these two nations trade with each other. It will become potentially the greatest trading relationship the world has ever seen .” Khambata also addressed the effect of sanctions and tariffs on international trade and arbitration. He said that unilateral economic measures had historically failed and were eventually withdrawn after causing conflict. “ Unilateral sanctions or tariffs have never worked. items.title: Cult.fit co-founder Rishabh Telang moves Karnataka High Court to quash forgery FIR ahead of IPO
items.summary: Weeks after fitness platform Cult.fit filed its draft papers for an initial public offering (IPO), its co-founder Rishabh Telang has moved the Karnataka High Court to quash a criminal case recently lodged against him by his brother-in-law [Rishabh Telang Vs State] Justice M Nagaprasanna on Tuesday issued notice to the State and complainant Deepak Poduval at whose instance the FIR against Telang was lodged. They were asked to file their responses to Telang's plea. However, the Court did not pass any interim order staying the investigation in the FIR. During the hearing, the Court noted that the police had issued Telang a notice under Section 35 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and that there was no immediate apprehension of arrest. The matter will be heard next on September 2. According to the complaint, Telang subsequently excluded him from the management of the company and diverted its business, customers, goodwill and revenue to Cultfit Healthcare Private Limited, which was incorporated in August 2016. items.title: CBSE OSM row: Supreme Court refuses to direct reopening of re-evaluation portal for class XII answer sheets
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday refused to direct the reopening of the CBSE Class XII examination verification and re-evaluation portal for students with grievances over the evaluation of their answer sheets through the On-Screen Marking (OSM) system. A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed the portal had already been opened for all candidates for a specified period and that reopening it could trigger lakhs of fresh claims. "If you don't use the bus, you miss the bus," CJI Kant said. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The Court was hearing a petition challenging the manner in which CBSE introduced the OSM system for evaluation of answer sheets. The plea pointed out that OSM was implemented for the first time in 2026 and that teachers were not provided formal training before its implementation. The plea alleged that the introduction of digital scanning resulted in several irregularities, including certain pages of answer sheets not being scanned, illegible scans and answers or pages not being evaluated. The petitioner claimed that these errors led to arbitrary evaluation and in some cases, non-evaluation of answer sheets. On August 14, the Court had asked the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) to explore ways to protect the interests of students facing difficulties in entrance-based admissions due to their low scores. Today, counsel representing the petitioner said that they were seeking only for a week's extension of the re-evaluation application window. items.title: Allahabad HC asks State to enhance compensation for dependents of advocates under financial aid scheme
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court has directed the State government to consider enhancing the amount of compensation payable to the dependents of deceased advocates [ Jyotima v State of UP and 2 Others ]. A Division Bench of Justice Ajit Kumar and Justice Garima Prashad noted that the compensation under the ‘Financial Assistance Scheme for Advocates’ was fixed at ₹5 lakh in 2015 and since then, the corpus for the scheme has swollen to ₹330 crore from ₹20 crore. However, the Court observed that the compensation amount has remained static at ₹5 lakh. It thus called upon the government to consider increasing the compensation amount. “Let the Government come up with an affidavit as to what amount it proposes to enhance towards the compensation under financial assistance scheme, and we leave it to the wisdom of the State Government. If a proper affidavit in this regard is not filed by the next date fixed, this Court will be compelled to take a serious view of the matter,” the Court directed. Justice Ajit Kumar and Justice Garima Prashad The Court was hearing a petition moved by a widow of an advocate for payment of interest on account of the delayed disposal of her application seeking compensation of ₹5 lakh. She had applied for compensation in 2020 but the same was paid only in 2025. On July 7, the Court took a serious view of the delay and directed Member Secretary of the Uttar Pradesh Advocate Welfare Fund Trustee Society, Lucknow (trust), to explain the delay in disbursing the compensation to the needy and eligible dependents of deceased advocates. In response, the Court was told that applications under the scheme are routed through the Bar Council of Uttar Pradesh and that due to non-compliance with relevant guidelines, the applications either remain pending there or are even sent back to the State Bar Council for further verification and compliances. At present, 1,207 applications are pending on account of such deficiencies. The Court criticised the Bar Council for delaying the verification of such applications. It noted that the council already has a roll of registered advocates and once a dependent moves an application for compensation, it should get all the forms duly filled up with all supporting documents and only then forward them to the trust for disbursement. “We fail to understand as to why the Bar Council sends to Trust such applications with insufficient details or forwards deficient application for not being accompanied by relevant material documents t

items.title: Delhi High Court restrains FSSAI from cancelling ITC licence over 100% Atta, 0% Maida claims

items.title: Supreme Court grants protection from arrest to journalist Abhishek Upadhyay who reported on Ram Mandir donation theft
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday granted protection from arrest to journalist Abhishek Upadhyay, who reported about Ram Mandir donation theft in Ayodhya, in a road rage case filed against him. The Court also sought the response of the Uttar Pradesh government to the plea filed by Upadhyay to quash the case against him. items.title: Doesn't deserve to be public prosecutor: Supreme Court on TN law officer who withheld key evidence
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday sought the Tamil Nadu government’s response to strong remarks made by the Madras High Court against a public prosecutor who failed to place crucial evidence before the trial court in a rape case. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta issued notice on a challenge by the public prosecutor against the observations made by the High Court in its order. However, while doing so, it questioned the prosecutor's credibility for failing to produce an accident register before the trial court despite the register being part of his case diary. items.title: Not essential religious practice: Allahabad High Court rejects Muslim student’s plea to wear hijab in school
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently rejected a Muslim student’s plea seeking directions to allow her to wear a (hijab) headscarf in addition to the uniform prescribed by her school [Sukaina Rizvi v State of UP and Others] In a judgment delivered on August 21, a bench of Justice JJ Munir and Justice Indrajeet Shukla noted that High Courts have been unanimous in their opinion that wearing a headscarf is not essential part of the Islamic faith for a woman. items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently questioned why Indian women are expected to take permission from members of the matrimonial home to visit their own parents' home. Justice Chillakur Sumalatha said that wives cannot be expected to solely do household work. "This Court does not understand why an Indian woman is required to take permission of all present at her matrimonial home to fulfil her basic desire of visiting her parents house as and when she wish and feels to go. The duty of taking care of parents vests upon the son or the daughter and not on the son-in-law or daughter-in-law, the Court added. items.title: Everybody is sitting in luxury: Delhi HC pans authorities over inaction in Yamuna cleaning issue

items.title: Rajasthan High Court takes suo motu cognizance of welfare of Gen Z, Gen Alpha and Gen Beta
items.summary: The Rajasthan High Court on Monday suo motu initiated a public interest litigation (PIL) to examine issues concerning the education, health, safety and future of children and youngsters belonging to Gen Z, Gen Alpha and Gen Beta generations [IN RE: “In the matter of Welfare and Future of Generation Gen-Z, Gen-Alpha and Gen-Beta”] . Justice Anoop Kumar Dhand held that three generations would be responsible for leading the country in the coming years. Underlining the broader responsibility towards children, the Court stated that the State must ensure they are equipped to meet the challenges of a rapidly changing technological and social environment. “Children are future of a nation because they grow up to become its workforce, leaders and caretakers. How we, as a nation, care, teach and protect them today will decide the strength, safety and success of our country tomorrow. They are flowers of our national garden and it is our prime duty to protect these flowers,” observed the Court. Justice Anoop Kumar Dhand The Court said governments needed to address a range of challenges facing Gen Z. items.title: Madras HC orders probe into Teachers Recruitment Board officials for ignoring Supreme Court ruling
items.summary: The Madras High Court has ordered a probe to identify Teachers Recruitment Board (TRB) officials responsible for ignoring a Supreme Court ruling on how reserved-category backlog vacancies must be filled [ Teachers Recruitment Board v. C Vijayalakshmi and connected cases ]. A Bench of Justices SM Subramaniam and Krishnaswamy Govindarajan directed the TRB Chairperson to conduct an inquiry and identify the officials responsible for failing to implement the Supreme Court’s ruling in State of Tamil Nadu v. K Shobana . The Court added that departmental disciplinary proceedings should be initiated against the officials, if necessary. “ The manner in which the provisional selection list for the post of P.G. Assistant (Economics) was issued shows that the Teachers Recruitment Board had disrespected the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court which is deprecated ,” the Court said. The dispute arose from a 2021 notification issued by the TRB for the recruitment of postgraduate assistant teachers in Economics. The candidates before the Court participated in the recruitment process and were included in the first provisional selection list published on September 14, 2022. However, their names were removed when the TRB issued a second provisional list on October 13, 2022. The candidates challenged the revised list, arguing that the recruitment body had incorrectly applied Section 27(f) of the Tamil Nadu Government Servants (Conditions of Service) Act, 2016. The provision deals with vacancies reserved for various communities and the treatment of backlog vacancies. In K Shobana , the Supreme Court held that candidates belonging to reserved categories, who qualify on their own merit, must be placed against General Turn vacancies. Such candidates cannot be pulled down from the general merit list and adjusted against backlog vacancies reserved for their communities. The Supreme Court had clarified that the word “first” in Section 27(f) only requires backlog vacancies to be filled before the current reserved vacancies. It does not mean that backlog vacancies must be filled before completing the General Turn merit list. Therefore, the provision relating to reservation becomes applicable only after candidates selected on merit have been accommodated in the General Turn. The TRB admitted before the High Court that it had not followed the Shobana ruling while preparing the second provisional selection list. It claimed that the decision had been applied only to an earlier recruitment

items.title: Transgender person moves Kerala High Court alleging denial of entry to Sabarimala
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Monday sought the State government's response to a plea filed by a transgender devotee alleging denial of permission to enter Sabarimala temple due to her gender [Sathyashri Sharmila Rehemathali v State of Kerala & ors]. A bench of Justice Gopinath P and Justice S Manu issued notice to the State and posed the matter to September 3 for further consideration. Justice Gopinath P and Justice S Manu The petition was filed by Sathyashri Sharmila Rehemathali, who identifies as a transgender woman and claims that she is a devote and a regular pilgrim to Sabarimala. According to the petition, Sharmila reached Pamba on August 20 to get Lord Ayyappa's darshan, after observing the required Vratham and carrying her Irumudi (sacred rituals undertaken by devotees). However, around 3:30 PM, she was stopped during a police inspection near the Pamba Ganapathi Temple and informed that she would not be permitted to proceed uphill because she was a transgender person. She further pointed out that she had previously visited the temple on January 3 and April 15, 2026, and had been permitted to complete her pilgrimage and receive darshan. The petitioner therefore approached the Court, challenging the sudden restriction on her entry to the temple solely on account of her transgender identity as arbitrary and unconstitutional. She also relied on Section 3(e) of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, which prohibits denial of or unfair treatment in, access to public places and religious institution, stating that the authorities failed to enforce the statutory protections. The petitioner has sought, among other reliefs, permission to undertake the pilgrimage to Sabarimala and offer prayers, besides direction to the state government to disclose and publish any circular or notification that restricts the entry of transgender devotees. items.summary: A court in Kashmir has issued a show-cause notice to a tehsildar asking him to explain why appropriate legal action should not be initiated against him over unauthorised use of a red beacon/warning light and multiple-toned siren on his official vehicle. Special Mobile Magistrate (Traffic) Shabir Ahmad Malik passed the order on an application filed by one Muzaffar Ahmad through advocates Sajad Mohi-ud-din and Haroon Rashid. After examining the application and examining the material placed on record, the Court observed that a prima facie case was made out warranting an inquiry into the factual position. The Court directed SSP Traffic Rural Kashmir to physically inspect the official vehicle belonging to tehsildar Tariq Ahmad Sheikh and ascertain whether his vehicle is fitted with a red/blue beacon light and/or multi-toned siren. The Court further directed that if an unauthorised beacon or multiple-toned siren is found, the inspecting authority shall immediately seize/remove the same and initiate action under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 and other relevant law. items.title: Court fees should be refunded to litigants whose cases can't be heard: Madras High Court
items.summary: The Madras High Court recently observed that litigants are “consumers of justice” and they are entitled to a refund of court fees paid if their case cannot be heard because of maintainability [Murugavel Vs Pichai] A Bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and KK Ramakrishnan said that a litigant who mistakenly approaches a court lacking jurisdiction does not receive the service for which the court fee was paid. “Jurist Upendra Baxi would call litigants as consumers of justice. Litigants come to the courts for adjudication of their lis. If the matter could not be taken up for adjudication at all because it was not maintainable in the first instance, the litigant did not receive any service. There has been a failure of consideration and a case for refund stands made out ,” the Court said. Justice GR Swaminathan The Bench made the observation while dealing with an appeal filed by one J Murugavel against an arbitral award passed in October 2024. Murugavel directly challenged the arbitral award before the High Court under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. However, the Court noted that Section 37 only provides for appeals against specified orders and does not permit a direct appeal against a final arbitral award. Such an award can only be challenged through a petition under Section 34 of the Act, the Court explained. “ Unfortunately, this appeal came to be filed and what is worse, it was numbered also ,” the Bench remarked while closing the appeal as not maintainable. Murugavel’s counsel then requested that the court fee paid for filing the appeal be refunded. The Court examined Section 70 of the Tamil Nadu Court-Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1955, which states that a fee paid by mistake or inadvertence “shall” be refunded. It concluded that the filing of the appeal arose from a failure to properly understand the scope of Section 37 and therefore, amounted to inadvertence. The Court clarified that inadvertence could include ignorance of the law. The Bench also said that a court fee could not be retained when the court was legally incapable of granting the relief sought. Since an appeal against the final arbitral award did not lie under Section 37, acceptance of the court fee for such an appeal was without the authority of law, it added. “ If refund is not ordered, there would be unjust enrichment for the State ,” the judgment stated. items.title: MP/MLA endorsement for women to get ₹2,500 financial assistance a policy decision, did not "come out of sky: Delhi govt to HC
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Monday said that it could declare the Delhi Lakshmi Yojana arbitrary if even one deserving woman is excluded from the scheme because of lack of endorsement from the local Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) or the Member of Parliament (MP). Under the Delhi Lakshmi Yojana, the Delhi government provides financial assistance of ₹2,500 per month to eligible women. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia today questioned the rationale behind the condition requiring MP or MLA endorsement. “What is the objective you are trying to achieve by this? Suppose you don’t know any MP or MLA? If even one person is left out [because of the condition], then the scheme is arbitrary. What is the objective you are trying to achieve through this condition? There are thousands of ways you can identify people,” the Bench remarked. Delhi High Court If even one person is left out [because of the condition], then the scheme is arbitrary. Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia Additional Solicitor General (ASG) Chetan Sharma appeared for the Delhi government and stated that the government took the policy decision to introduce the condition to ensure that no persona non grata (unwelcome person) gets the benefit. Sharma said that the government wants to file a reply in the case and that over six lakh people have received the benefit under the scheme. “Your lordships may not agree with us, but we are entitled to say how the cabinet has seen it and what the position is in other States. This has not come out of the sky. There is something we want to place on record, we will do it,” he said. The High Court said that the wisdom of the government has to be tested on the fundamental rights under the Constitution. It added that there are many other means to ascertain that a persona non grata does not get the benefit. “Wisdom of the government has to be tested on Part 3 [of the Constitution. You can’t go away by saying this. Every decision, Mr Sharma, has to go the test of Part III (of the Constitution),” the Court said. Sharma replied that the government was not "going away" from the issue and that it will file a reply. The Court has now given the government 10 days to file its affidavit, explaining the rationale behind the condition. items.title: Google-Adani data centre will not affect environment: Andhra Pradesh government tells High Court
items.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government on Monday told the Andhra Pradesh High Court that it is taking every step to ensure that the construction of the proposed Google-Adani data centres in Vishakapatnam does not affect the environment [ Bolisetty Satyanarayana v. The State of Andhra Pradesh ]. The counsel representing the State government made the submission before a bench of Chief Justice Lisa Gill and Justice Challa Gunaranjan in response to a public interest litigation (PIL) petition raising several concerns about the multi-billion-dollar project, including its potential impact on the environment. " Counsel for the State submits that care and caution is being exercised in ensuring that all steps are taken within the parameters of law and due care is being taken for protection of the environment ," the Court recorded in the order passed after the hearing today. Apart from environmental concerns, the PIL filed by environmental activist and Jal Biradari National Convenor Bolisetty Satyanarayana contended that 160 acres of the land allotted for data centres was temple land which belongs to the Simhachalam Devasthanam. The same should not have been transferred for commercial purposes and ought to be restored to the temple, the petitioner contended. He also argued that while the government has been claiming that the project would strengthen India's digital economy, the data centres will not be storing or processing Indian data. The petitioner also submitted that there was a forest and a water reservoir right next to the site for the data centres. Both are ecologically sensitive locations and construction could cause irreversible damage to ecological balance and biodiversity in the area, it was argued. He further submitted that Visakhapatnam has been suffering major water crises since 2015 and construction of these data centres would only exacerbate the situation. Despite these concerns, the government had not done any environmental impact studies, the PIL petitioner argued. The Court should issue directions to halt further construction until comprehensive studies are undertaken, it was submitted. The PIL will be heard again next week by which time the State government and its various authorities are expected to file their respective counter-affidavits. items.title: Karnataka HC rejects State's plea to cancel bail granted to BJP MLA Byrathi Basavaraj in murder case
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Monday dismissed the State government's petition seeking cancellation of bail granted to BJP MLA Byrathi Basavaraj, who is an accused in the murder of rowdy-sheeter Shivaprakash alias Biklu Shiva [State of Karnataka v. BA Basavaraja] . Justice M Nagaprasanna dismissed the State's petition, declining to interfere with the bail granted to Basavaraj on March 12 this year. Justice M Nagaprasanna Karnataka High Court issues notice to BJP MLA Byrathi Basavaraj on State's plea to cancel his bail in murder case The case arises from the murder of Biklu Shiva, who was allegedly attacked by a group of assailants in front of his mother's house in Bengaluru on July 15, 2025. The complaint was lodged by Vijay Lakshmi, the mother of the deceased. According to the complaint, Shiva was attacked at around 8 pm by around 8-9 unidentified persons. The incident was allegedly witnessed by two persons, following which the complaint was registered and a first information report (FIR) was lodged. The investigation was initially conducted by the Bharati Nagar Police and was subsequently transferred to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) pursuant to a State government order. After taking over the investigation, the CID sought permission to invoke provisions of the Karnataka Control of Organised Crime Act (KCOCA) in the case. The competent authority granted permission for invoking the provisions on August 2, 2025. Basavaraj challenged the invocation of KCOCA, which was subsequently allowed by the High Court by an order dated December 19, 2025. He was initially remanded to police custody for one week and was thereafter remanded to judicial custody. In February, Basavaraj had approached the Supreme Court seeking anticipatory bail, to no avail. The trial court later granted bail on the ground that the material cited against Basavaraj did not appear to be strong . items.title: Gauhati High Court closes PIL on adjournment reforms after HC notification addresses concerns
items.summary: The Gauhati High Court recently closed a public interest litigation (PIL) petition filed seeking uniform guidelines on adjournments and mandatory digital upload of court records. A Division Bench of Justices Michael Zothankhuma and Arun Dev Choudhury on August 10 noted that the petitioner himself submitted that an intervening administrative notification issued by the High Court Registry had addressed the concerns raised in the matter. "Mr. R. Singh, petitioner-in-person submits that in view of the Notification No. 21 dated 23.03.2026, issued by the Registrar General, Gauhati High Court, nothing survives to be adjudicated in the present Public Interest Litigation (PIL). Accordingly, the instant PIL stands closed," the Court said. Justice Michael Zothankhuma Reetam Singh, an advocate enrolled with the Bar Council of Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim, had filed the PIL in 2024. He cited his own experience in a case filed under the Negotiable Instruments Act and a money suit to argue that adjournments were being routinely granted by trial courts on inadequate grounds. This violated the scheme of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC), and of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC), he contended. He sought directions for a strict adjournment regime limiting adjournments to rare, substantiated circumstances, imposition of costs on counsel seeking unjustified adjournments, a uniform date-allocation system across subordinate courts on the pattern followed by the High Court, and the mandatory online upload of daily order sheets. These measures were intended to ensure transparency for litigants who otherwise depend entirely on their counsel for information about case proceedings. The petition also sought the constitution of a committee to frame adjournment guidelines, a digital date-allocation system to be developed in consultation with technical experts from IIT Guwahati, and the framing of disciplinary rules against counsel who misuse the adjournment process. In the meantime, the new criminal laws came into effect in India, from July 1, 2024. The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) replaced the CrPC. In March 2026, the High Court's registry issued a notification for the implementation of these new criminal laws. It emphasised that trial courts should adhere to the two-adjournment limit under Section 346(2) of the BNSS. items.title: Supreme Court restores Congress leader’s election petition challenging BJP MP Kripanath Mallah’s 2024 poll win
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday set aside the Gauhati High Court’s dismissal of an election petition challenging Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Member of Parliament Kripanath Mallah’s victory in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. [ Hafiz Rashid Ahmed Choudhury v. Kripanath Mallah and Others ] Congress candidate and Senior Advocate Hafiz Rashid Ahmed Choudhury had challenged Mallah's election on the ground that the BJP leader had employed corrupt practices to win the elections from Assam's Karimganj parliamentary constituency. In April 2025, however, the Gauhati High Court, dismissed Choudhury's petition on noting certain defects in it. The High Court did not go into the merits of the case. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran today allowed Chowdhury's appeal against this ruling. The top court held that the defects cited by the High Court to dismiss Chowdhury's petition at the threshold were not fatal. Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice Vinod Chandran The defect flagged by the High Court concerned a Form 25 affidavit filed by Choudhury in support of his allegations that Mallah had committed corrupt practices. The original affidavit in the High Court’s record appeared to have been affirmed before a commissioner of affidavits. However, the copy served on Mallah did not carry any endorsement showing such affirmation. The top court today held that this omission did not justify dismissing the entire election petition. " Obviously, the defect under Section 83 does not entail peremptory dismissal under Section 86 of the RoP Act ,” the Supreme Court said. Therefore, it directed the High Court to verify whether the original affidavit contained the required attestation. If it did, the High Court was directed to consider the petition on merits, including by examining the allegations of corrupt practices. If the required attestation was absent, the Court said Choudhury should not be permitted to pursue the allegations of corrupt practices. However, the High Court must still examine other independent grounds, if any, raised in the petition, the Supreme Court added. “ Suffice it to request the High Court to verify and if due attestation of the affirmation on oath is available, proceed with the matter on merits and if not available, not to permit the allegation of corrupt practices to be urged and proceed with the consideration on the merits of the other grounds, if any are pleaded ,” the Court said. items.title: Forensic evidence should aid cases, not create more burden for survivors: Ex-ASG Pinky Anand
items.summary: Better forensic practices should strengthen cases before courts without creating an additional burden of proof for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence, former Additional Solicitor General of India Pinky Anand said at a training workshop in Goa on Saturday. The day-long workshop, held on August 22, focused on implementing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for the collection, preservation, chain of custody and presentation of forensic evidence in cases of sexual assault, rape and child abuse. “Better forensic practice must strengthen the case that reaches the court. It must never become a fresh threshold of belief that survivors are asked to clear,” said Anand. The SOPs were formally launched by Anand at the Police Headquarters in Panjim on April 26 last year, marking World DNA Day. They were subsequently expanded to include the handling of forensic evidence in cases involving child abuse. The workshop brought together police officers, prosecutors, judicial officers, medical practitioners and other professionals involved in the investigation and prosecution of sexual and gender-based violence and child abuse cases. A key focus was a victim-centred approach to investigation. The participants discussed how survivors could be treated with dignity and sensitivity while ensuring that evidence is collected in accordance with due process. The sessions also covered practical aspects of collecting and preserving forensic material, maintaining its chain of custody and presenting it before courts. Medical experts discussed factors affecting the reliability and evidentiary value of forensic material. Legal practitioners examined how such evidence should be presented in court. SOP Training Workshop, Goa Speaking at the workshop, Anand said forensic evidence in sexual violence cases can disappear within hours. She cited instances where a survivor may bathe, clothes may be washed or a crime scene may be cleaned. She stressed that procedural discipline was critical to ensuring forensic evidence could withstand scrutiny in court. " The science was sound throughout; what failed, for a time, was the discipline around it — which is precisely what a Standard Operating Procedure exists to secure, from the first responder at the scene to an unbroken chain of custody that can withstand cross-examination," said Anand. items.title: Supreme Court stays BCI order debarring former judicial officer from legal practice
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday stayed a Bar Council of India (BCI) order permanently debarring a Madhya Pradesh-based advocate, Narendra Kumar Jain from practising law. Jain had earlier served as a judicial officer before resigning from the post [ Narendra Kumar Jain v. Bar Council of India ]. The BCI had passed an order in July, debarring Jain from practice over allegations of professional misconduct arising from repeated, persistent, and unprovoked public attacks on the judiciary and individual judges. This order has now been challenged by Jain before the Supreme Court. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta today sought the BCI's response to Jain's plea and stayed the debarrment order for now. "Issue notice. In the meantime effect and operation of the impugned order will remain stayed," the Court said. items.title: Even 0.1% of amount spent for Nashik Kumbh Mela could save Marathi medium schools: Supreme Court Justice PB Varale
items.summary: Supreme Court Justice Prasanna B Varale recently raised serious concerns over the declining budget for education in Maharashtra, contrasting the closure of State-run Marathi medium schools with the massive public expenditure on events like the Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha or Nashik Kumbh Mela. The judge was speaking at an event organised by a high school in Dhule district of Maharashtra, where he had been a student for a few years. The event was an inauguration of 'smart classes'. In his address, Justice Varale highlighted how essential educational infrastructure continues to suffer despite grand government allocations for other initiatives. He referred to recent announcements regarding government expenditure on the Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha Kumbh Mela and major infrastructure corridors. “The government claims to allocate vast funds for various initiatives. I read elsewhere about ₹11,000 crore being allocated for a corridor project,” Justice Varale pointed out. He added that even a tiny fraction of such spending could revive hundreds of struggling educational institutions across the state. “I have no objection whatsoever to the thousands of crores being spent by the government on various development initiatives. However, if out of these thousands of crores of allocated funds, even just 0.1%—around ₹32 crore—were spent by the government, then 100 to 125 Marathi-medium schools that have closed down across the state would not have shut down." items.title: Actor Devan to join Vijay’s TVK after quitting BJP, says he was offered Kerala chief post
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Malayalam actor and politician S Devan on Monday, August 24, said he has decided to join Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), the party led by Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay. Devan recently resigned as the Kerala state vice-president of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). He said TVK representatives approached him after his resignation, and that he accepted the invitation following preliminary discussions. A formal announcement about his joining the party is expected after Devan meets Vijay in Chennai on September 10. Devan told the media that TVK had offered him the post of president of its Kerala unit. “I raised certain issues in 2004, and that is exactly what Vijay is raising now. There are certain similarities between Joseph Vijay and me in politics, and that is what attracted me to him,” Devan said. Devan said he entered politics with the aim of fighting corruption and communalism and creating a new political culture. “In 2004, I was the highest-paid villain in south India. I knew that if I entered politics, it would affect my film career. So I made that sacrifice and entered politics,” he said. Devan began his political career during his college days with the Kerala Students Union (KSU), the student wing of the Congress party. He formally entered electoral politics in 2004, when he formed the Kerala People’s Party. He contested the 2004 Wadakkanchery bye-election and the 2006 Assembly election from Thiruvananthapuram on the party’s ticket, but lost both elections. In 2020, Devan renamed and relaunched the party as the Nava Kerala People’s Party. The party merged with the BJP in 2021, following which Devan was appointed vice-president of the BJP's Kerala unit. Devan resigned from the BJP on August 15, announcing his decision at a function at the Kanichukulangara Devi temple in Alappuzha, which is managed by the Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Yogam. At the event, Devan said he had felt a lack of “space” and meaningful work during his nearly five years in the BJP. He also accused the BJP’s Kerala unit of moving away from the ideals of social justice espoused by social reformer Sree Narayana Guru.

Around 9.30 pm on Sunday, August 23, Sangeetha got a call from her mother M Kalavathi. “I’ll be late getting home, you have dinner and go to sleep,” she told her. Earlier in the evening, Kalavathi had stepped out of their house in Padi Puthunagar of Chennai’s Anna Nagar West Extension to go to church. Less than two hours later, around 11.20 pm, Sangeetha’s phone rang again. This time, it was the Ayanavaram police calling to ask her to identify the photo of a woman they had found unconscious in a rainwater-filled pit. She had “fainted”, Sangeetha was told. That woman, who was later declared dead at the Kilpauk Medical College Hospital (KMCH), was Kalavathi. Passersby had found the 59-year-old woman unconscious in a pit near the Anna Nagar Tower Metro station in Chennai and alerted the police. With the help of the public, they pulled her out and took her to KMCH, where doctors declared her brought dead. The police told the family that when onlookers tried to lift her out of the pit, they had experienced minor electric shocks, raising suspicion that Kalavathi had been electrocuted after falling into the pit. “The Thirumangalam police said she had slipped into the pit and got electrocuted. Her body was sent to the Kilpauk Medical College Hospital mortuary for post-mortem examination. items.title: DD News promoted E20 using seven pro-govt farmer leaders without disclosing their ties
items.summary: A nationwide debate is raging over ethanol-blended petrol, or E20, with motorists complaining of lower mileage and alleged engine damage. The government, meanwhile, has stuck to a central defence: E20 is good for farmers. DD News has been an enthusiastic vehicle for that message. Since May, the public broadcaster has aired more than 50 explainers, debates and ground reports promoting E20. But last month, it went a step further, publishing videos of seven farmer leaders on its official social media accounts, all making essentially the same case: ethanol blending is driving farmers’ progress. There was something else these seven had in common. All were already supporters of the Modi government and its policies. Several had backed the three farm laws at the centre of the 2020–21 farmers’ protest, and some had openly opposed the agitation. So, in other words, as criticism of E20 mounted, DD News turned to seven farmer leaders with established pro-government positions to bolster its case for ethanol blending, without disclosing those affiliations to its audience. The seven were K P Singh Thainuan of Gaon Kisan Unnayan, Ashok Balyan of the Peasant Welfare Association, Krishanveer Chaudhary of the Bharatiya Krishak Samaj, Dharmendra Chaudhary of the Bharatiya Kisan Union (Chaudhary Charan Singh), Rampal Jat of the Kisan Mahapanchayat, K Sai Reddy of the Bharatiya Kisan Sangh, and Vinod Anand, a member of the government’s MSP committee. All seven videos were published back-to-back on the DD News YouTube channel on July 28, and the messaging across them was strikingly uniform, framing dissent itself as unpatriotic. ‘Anti-national’ Krishanveer Chaudhary called opponents of ethanol blending “anti-national,” saying farmers were shifting from being annadata , or food providers, to urjadata , or energy providers, and that “opposing it cannot be justified in any way”. K P Singh Thainuan dismissed concerns as “entirely baseless” and tied ethanol expansion to the government’s “Viksit Bharat 2047” vision. Ashok Balyan claimed sugarcane, paddy, and maize farmers were benefiting substantially. K Sai Reddy went further, alleging that “the oil lobby, certain NGOs, and foreign forces” were behind the opposition, declaring that “anyone opposing ethanol is opposing the farmer”. Vinod Anand called the ethanol program “farmer-centric, administratively implementable, environmentally sustainable, and economically viable,” and likewise branded critics “anti-nationals”. items.title: Kerala: Temple worker alleges suspension after daughter marries outside caste
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A temple worker in Kannur has alleged that he was suspended from his duties after his daughter married a man from another caste. CV Rajan, a 58-year-old resident of Karivellur, who has worked as an upakarmi (temple assistant) at the Karivelloor Muchilot Bhagavathi Temple for three decades, has approached the Malabar Devaswom Board with a complaint against the suspension. The allegation, meanwhile, has been disputed by the temple authorities, who have cited alleged violations of temple practices and misconduct as the reasons for the action. Rajan's family has been associated with the temple for generations, and he took up the job after his father. He told TNM he has not been working at the temple for about four months now. He was initially suspended in March and asked to explain the allegations against him by April 1. The temple later issued a formal suspension order effective June 15, stating that his explanation was unsatisfactory. Rajan’s daughter married a man from the Pothuval community on March 15. Rajan belongs to the Vaniya community, which is classified as an Other Backward Class (OBC) in Kerala, while Pothuval is classified under the general category, according to the state’s classification.
